description: Folded GDN decode (gdn_conv_recurrent_update) from the validated shared-norm probe: the l2 scales of q and k are closed once per token by the first thread pair (the original ascending 64-term FP32 sums and lane-1 exchange), q and k are re-read from LDS by their consumers instead of held across the delta-rule update, and every BF16 intermediate, ascending FP32 accumulation, anchor/state semantic, conv padding guard and the INT8 quantiser epilogue is unchanged. One authoritative payload also owns the engine scratch: the row emits a real 256-thread counter-clear kernel on the caller's stream before every main dispatch, so reused and uninitialized scratch cannot stall the last-arriver protocol; no hipMalloc, hipMemset or sync. launch and describe carry the same two dispatches from one body (20 arguments, 224 packed bytes, compile-time asserted). Fixed served specialization: head_k/head_v 128, conv width 4, fp32 anchor state, INT8 quant output, NT1 <= 16 MiB state flood, 1..16 tokens per sequence and N*Hg <= 4096 counters; everything else is refused at selection or at launch, so the row claims no generic coverage. Priority 60 is intra-plugin only. The incoming convolution padding guard (cslot < 0) is explicit in the fork; the frozen row keeps the same guard, and the NUL-corrupted libr4d MoE source is untouched. Not a gate PASS or an engine speed claim.
